rationale: Complete 52-file v6-to-upstream inline-encryption refresh and its documentation examined. Native crypto profiles/request contexts implement pointer-identity keyslots, DUN-width capabilities, request preparation/release and front/back merge continuity. Native fallback saves completion state and clears submitted crypto context, supports RAW keys only, and uses synchronous ciphers and current initialization cleanup; preserve e2fc28947c38 allocation rescue and c45528667984 metadata-skip cloning. Native fscrypt retains SB_INLINECRYPT, all-device capability checks, current prepared-key publication and per-data-unit geometry; historical NOFS wrapper is superseded by upstream 9dad5feb49a5. Native F2FS keeps physical plus crypto merge checks, compression crypto selection and submitted-folio indices. Keep native DM table profiles and monotonic capabilities, plus the already justified default-key target. Native UFS profile/custom-profile model replaces the historical crypto-vops interfaces; UFS host/core files remain LTS and no physical-platform addition is made. Old source interface names, embedded profile layout and hash/DUN packing are not compatibility requirements for historical binaries.

subject: FROMGIT: f2fs: fix race of pending_pages in decompression
rationale: The historical patch separates reused decompression/verity counters and introduces per-bio verity policy. Native LTS has replaced that design: alloc_dic initializes remaining_pages once plus refcnt=1 and a per-cluster need_verity; end_read_compressed_page decrements remaining_pages to trigger decompression, which enqueues cluster verification only after completion. It never resets remaining_pages for verity. Pagecache completion owns one reference until verification/unlock, each compressed bio page has a separate reference, and mixed-bio verification skips compressed pages already verified by the cluster. The native failure and context-release paths are retained. Full historical patch, current alloc/read/decompress/verify/free paths and struct lifetime comments were examined; do not revive the superseded counter/API design. Evidence: complete local ACK patch and named LTS/port functions; SECURITY.md. No remote access or runtime test.

subject: ANDROID: dm-user: Fail the IO if there is no daemon
rationale: Retain the configurable initial 4000ms no-daemon grace period and immediate failure after the last daemon channel closes. Adapt ownership: initialize work once per message, detach/claim before cancel, have callbacks skip detached entries, cancel unconditionally before handing ownership to a channel or final destruction, and rearm with mod_delayed_work on last close even after an earlier callback returned while a daemon existed. Prevent pool waits under the lock required by progress, and reject pool construction failure. The old per-message delayed flag and cached-next teardown assumptions are not retained. Seven negative controls cover the focused regression hazards; actual kernel concurrency is untested. Evidence: evidence/dm-user-local-review.json; SECURITY.md: dm-user timeout ownership and allocation progress. Local snapshot.cpp and snapuserd control-device protocol are positive consumers; SDK OTA use is unconfirmed. Only local sources were used. The follow-up pending-work guard prevents freeing a message with a rearmed callback still queued.

subject: Revert "ANDROID: overlayfs: override_creds=off option bypass creator_cred"
rationale: This intermediate removal was followed by ad8f22c703cf, itself removed in the final history. The five historical credential-bypass versions and their removals were compared through their unique changed lines and the complete final 8e21ce25c1f9 removal. Final ACK and native LTS no longer have config.override_creds or the old module parameter/override_creds=off enum option. Keep native stashed-credential and current-task permission checking. Positive pinned GrapheneOS evidence: fs_mgr uses mount(2), CheckOverlayfs adds userxattr only, init SetupOverlays executes overlay_remounter, and its explicit userdebug/eng SELinux domain remounts overlays with permissions for the underlying partitions. This is a concrete replacement for the old caller-credential bypass, not an absence-of-consumer inference. The modern upstream override_creds flag records mount credentials with the new mount API; it is not the historical bypass. No remount/SELinux runtime test was run. Retain newer LTS cross-superblock source-credential checks, dentry lifetime fixes and backing-file LSM state.
evidence: SECURITY.md: OverlayFS history and native permission model

rationale: Full LTS and normalized ACK deltas, swapcache/fault/shmem/zswap-writeback and reclaim callers reviewed. All timing-end callers retain a folio reference through submission; 14b3570de295 initializes independent timing cookies. Default-false read replacement leaves native full-folio bio setup, task reference, completion status and unlock unchanged; a trusted replacing callback must supply the full folio contents or error and perform completion/unlock, with the provided device-relative start-sector adjustment. Keep separate read/write capabilities for source customization; 14b3570de295 makes read dispatch and both cacheless callers test only the read bit. Ordinary swapon still sets both bits, and filesystem I/O keeps precedence. Extracted actual dispatch functions pass 387 flag/callback/early-completion/PSI-cleanup cases with host shims and UBSan, including the old write-only false match. Native write errors redirty/clear reclaim/end writeback and read errors leave folios not uptodate before unlocking. Native zeromap partial-folio failure, zswap failures, and PSI/delay cleanup remain. No actual block I/O, kernel PSI, fault race or callback execution tested. Complete header delta reviewed against page_io, swap_state, vmscan and kernel/power/swap.c. Separate read/write bit definitions retain the combined setter and do not change userspace swap flags; 14b3570de295 uses the read bit consistently in read and cacheless paths. Added reclaim_pages/__reclaim_pages and swap_cache_del_folio declarations match retained generic source APIs and their reviewed list/folio ownership. alloc_swapdev_block declaration matches the existing hibernation implementation/export and its callers; no hibernation platform enablement is added. subject: ANDROID: rust_binder: priority inheritance
rationale: Retain Rust Binder priority inheritance for Android libbinder scheduler-policy/minimum-priority/inherit-RT flags, matching the configured optional Rust driver and native Binder semantics. Adapt node decoding to sign-extend the wire priority byte as C Binder does; negative nice values otherwise become large positive values. Clamp unsigned RLIMIT_RTPRIO to the legal maximum before signed conversion, preserving zero-limit fallback and preventing large limits from truncating negative. Preserve CAP_SYS_NICE checks, RLIMIT_NICE bounds, RESET_ON_FORK, process default priority, once-only thread selection, pending/abort restoration and the selected-thread saved priority. Keep the port comparison against the desired priority after RT suppression, matching native Binder; ACK boundary still compares against the original caller priority. Native scheduler implementation is not replaced by these Rust wrappers. Invalid node priorities remain subject to native scheduler validation; no new privilege is granted by an out-of-range value.
evidence: SECURITY.md: Rust Binder priority and trace interfaces

subject: ANDROID: rust_binder: add all tracepoints
rationale: Retain Binder-named trace events and callsites for Android atrace/Perfetto: local atrace explicitly requires transaction, received and allocation events, while Perfetto registers and parses them. Full patch reviewed, including Arc::DATA_OFFSET, runtime layout/accessors, page shrinker snapshots, return/command bounds checks and trace wrappers. Live Rust references protect synchronous pointer reads; page shrinker copies scalar pid/index before releasing locks and does not retain freed range pointers. Adapt diagnostic node_ptr to the user-supplied node address, translated_handle to the translated object, and page-range indices to byte offsets/sizes expected by native Binder tracing. Saturation/reversed-range handling affects diagnostics only. Derive C pointer offsets from their actual Rust containers. Task/transaction metadata is exposed through the existing tracefs access policy, not transaction payload data. Native LTS tracing implementation remains, with driver-selection event removal assessed separately; this decision does not finalize the dual-driver selector.
evidence: SECURITY.md: Rust Binder priority and trace interfaces

subject: ANDROID: vendor_hooks: Add hooks for binder proc transaction
rationale: Retain special-work availability/selection, proc transaction, looper exit, spawn, ioctl-end and read-list hooks. Initial outputs preserve native behavior: list NULL, nothing_to_do/force_spawn false, has_work derived from native queues, ret zero only after successful ioctl dispatch. Native failure gotos bypass ioctl_end. A trusted callback may suppress availability, redirect queues or exceed max_threads via force_spawn; preserve for requested source customization, documenting denial-of-service and memory/lifetime obligations rather than presenting hooks as permission checks. Custom lists must be valid nonempty, protected by proc inner lock and paired with teardown; no actual scheduler policy/SDK vendor consumer established.

subject: ANDROID: rust: fix overflow in rlimit_nice()
rationale: Retain the clamp of the unsigned RLIMIT_NICE value to 40 before signed conversion and subtraction. Configured Rust Binder Thread::do_set_priority calls this method for a fair-policy task without CAP_SYS_NICE. RLIM_INFINITY or an arbitrary high raw limit otherwise permits signed subtraction overflow and a kernel panic with Rust overflow checks. Values 1..40 map to nice 19..-20; zero maps to 20 and the Binder caller rejects it as unset. Limits above 40 grant no priority beyond the legal minimum nice. This is a concrete safety fix for the selected Android priority API; native LTS scheduler checks are not weakened by this change.
evidence: SECURITY.md: Rust publication, poll and priority helpers

subject: ANDROID: 16K: Introduce rust __page_*() helpers
rationale: Retain Rust page-size-compat bindings and helpers for ashmem mapping size checks. The local SDK goldfish x86_64_16k_cmdline.txt selects page_shift=14, and ashmem mmap uses __page_align. The C boot parser restricts the shift to supported values on a 4 KiB kernel and stores it read-only after initialization. The selected ashmem caller rejects zero or size>=usize::MAX>>1 before alignment, so its addition cannot overflow at the supported shifts; the generic helper is not a checked-overflow API for arbitrary usize input. This decision covers the Rust helper and module/binding registration, not the still-unresolved shared EOF semantics of the wider 16 KiB emulation family. No native LTS arithmetic or fault handling is reverted.

subject: UPSTREAM: rust: id_pool: do not immediately acquire new ids
rationale: Retain deferred ID acquisition via UnusedId holding an exclusive mutable IdPool borrow. Rust Binder insert_or_update_handle performs fallible reservations/rechecks before committing its handle; only acquire sets the bit. Dropping an unused token leaves the bit free, while the borrow prevents another safe mutable pool access from racing it. as_u32 is bounded by the pool MAX_LEN=i32::MAX invariant. Grow/shrink allocate outside the caller lock and revalidate before replacing/copying the bitmap. Native C bitmap bounds checks remain; this review does not independently certify all Binder lock interleavings.

subject: UPSTREAM: rust_binder: use bitmap for allocation of handles
rationale: Retain bitmap-backed per-process Binder handle allocation through the previously reviewed IdPool. It preserves manager-only handle zero, acquires a bit only after both tree insertions succeed, releases it when the corresponding reference is removed, and detects a bitmap/tree mismatch without returning an occupied handle. Tree/node storage is reserved before locking; growth and shrink allocation release node_refs and revalidate after reacquisition. The second by_node lookup handles concurrent insertion, while the unused reservation has not set its bit. Shrink failure leaves a valid old bitmap. This avoids linear tree walks at increasing handle counts; no benchmark from the historical message was reproduced or adopted as SDK evidence.

subject: BACKPORT: FROMGIT: f2fs: fix missing read bio submission on large folio error
rationale: On a later readahead folio failing before bio insertion, complete that folio and flush the earlier accumulated bio before returning; stop consuming readahead. Replace unlock/relock error clearing with the submission reference and sticky failures. Tests cover failures before insertion with order-0 and large folios, in immediate, forward and reverse completion orders. F2FS and IOSTAT are enabled by the SDK configuration. The supplied SDK data fstab uses ext4; actual use of this optional generic filesystem feature is unconfirmed, so preserve the ACK source/configuration contract conservatively rather than infer omission from missing consumers. No future platform is enabled. Implementation and validation details are in SECURITY.md and evidence/f2fs-largefolio-check.json; no mounted-filesystem or runtime verification.

rationale: Capture folio_nr_pages while the folio remains locked and referenced, before f2fs_folio_put. rationale: The SDK enables BLK_INLINE_ENCRYPTION_FALLBACK and DM_DEFAULT_KEY; native LTS __submit_bio invokes crypto preparation while current->bio_list is active, so recursive encrypted submissions can hold the resources an allocation awaits. subject: UPSTREAM: rust: poll: use kfree_rcu() for PollCondVar
rationale: Retain PollCondVarBox with an embedded RCU callback head for the configured Rust Binder process poll queue. subject: ANDROID: rust: dma-buf: Adds with_name() and export_name() accessors
rationale: Retain exporter_name and with_name for configured wrapfd fdinfo. The native dma_buf.exp_name contract explicitly says non-NULL and immutable; the Rust returned borrow is tied to the held buffer. Mutable name access is under the native name_lock and exposed only inside the closure, so an owned Rust borrow cannot escape the guard. Local wrap.rs uses the callback to format fdinfo. The callback runs under a spinlock and must not sleep; the API does not add a userspace name access bypass or change native replacement/free rules.

subject: ANDROID: rust: Adds support for using a spinlock inside an IRQ handler.
rationale: Retain SpinLockIrq and native irqsave/irqrestore C helpers for configured WrapFD asynchronous I/O completion and result collection. The state is pinned; the closure receives a non-Send guard, exclusively borrows data under the native spinlock and restores the saved flags after any normal return, including a returned error. The closure lifetime prevents escaping the guard or a reference: an extracted-method compile probe accepts an owned value and rejects three escape patterns. The selected caller clones its SharedContext Arc before completion can wake/drop request storage. Send/Sync bounds match protected-data requirements. SDK uses non-RT spinlock semantics; no actual IRQ/concurrency or panic-unwind test is claimed. Existing malformed documentation examples are not treated as compiled doctest evidence.

subject: ANDROID: rust: add anon_inodes related APIs
rationale: Retain the anon-inode file abstraction used by WrapFD, adapted in f744d35f5a43 to remove &File from the release callback. Native __fput invokes release after the last reference is gone, while File::from_raw_file requires a positive reference count; the ACK wrapper violated this and exposed a refcount-acquirable File during destruction.
